Kiriathaim of Moab
kir-ee-uh-THAY-im of MOH-ab
proper noun
Hebrew qiryāthayim, “double city” or “two cities,” from qiryāh, a city; a city of the plain built by Reuben, fallen again to Moab and brought under judgment.

Biblical Definition

Kiriathaim was a city of the level plateau east of Jordan, builded by the children of Reuben when they took their inheritance: “the children of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Kirjathaim” (Num 32:37). It is named among Reuben’s cities in the dividing of the land, “Kirjathaim, and Sibmah, and Zarethshahar in the mount of the valley” (Josh 13:19). In time it fell again into the hand of Moab, and so came under the LORD’s judgment with the rest of that land: “Woe unto Nebo! for it is spoiled: Kiriathaim is confounded and taken” (Jer 48:1). Ezekiel too marks it among the cities of Moab’s frontier given over to the children of the east: “Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim” (Eze 25:9). Thus a city once raised by a tribe of Israel passed to a heathen people and shared their fall, that none might presume upon a name once holy. The history of Kiriathaim preaches that a place, like a soul, may begin within the covenant and yet be lost to idolatry and pride if the LORD be forsaken. Let the believer hold fast his inheritance with reverence, build upon the true foundation, and not, like the cities of Reuben that drifted into Moab, exchange the worship of the living God for the high places of the heathen. What is once given of grace must be kept by grace, or it is taken and confounded.

Webster 1828 Definition

A city of the plain built by Reuben, fallen again to Moab and brought under the LORD’s judgment with the rest of that land.

KIRIATHAIM OF MOAB, a city of the level plateau east of Jordan, whose name signifies “double city.”

It was builded by the children of Reuben when they received their inheritance.

It is named among Reuben’s cities in the dividing of the land under Joshua.

In time it fell again to Moab and came under the LORD’s judgment.

It witnesses that a place once within the covenant may be lost to idolatry if the LORD be forsaken.

Key Scripture

Num 32:37 — "And the children of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Kirjathaim,"

Josh 13:19 — "And Kirjathaim, and Sibmah, and Zarethshahar in the mount of the valley,"

Jer 48:1 — "Against Moab thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Woe unto Nebo! for it is spoiled: Kiriathaim is confounded and taken: Misgab is confounded and dismayed."

Eze 25:9 — "Therefore, behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on his frontiers, the glory of the country, Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim,"

Modern Corruption

A city of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses that a place once within the covenant may be lost to idolatry and judged if the LORD be forsaken.

expand to see more

Kiriathaim is a city of the plain, builded by Reuben and afterward fallen to Moab, named under the LORD’s judgment. No movement of the present age has troubled to redefine it; the dictionary records it that the reader may mark a place once raised by a tribe of Israel which drifted into a heathen people’s pride and idolatry, and so was confounded and taken.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that what is given of grace must be kept by grace. Reuben built the city, but it slipped to Moab and shared Moab’s fall; so the soul that presumes upon a name once holy, yet forsakes the LORD for the high places, is confounded. Let the believer hold fast his inheritance with reverence and build upon the true foundation alone.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “double city,” Kiriathaim names a city of the plain built by Reuben and judged with Moab.

expand to see more

Kiriathaim of Moab — Hebrew qiryāthayim, “double city” or “two cities.”

It is from qiryāh, a city, in a dual form.

It was a city of the level plateau builded by the children of Reuben.

It fell again to Moab and was confounded and taken under judgment.

It is named among Moab’s frontier cities by Jeremiah and Ezekiel.

Usage

"Let the believer hold fast his inheritance, lest like Kiriathaim it slip from the covenant to the heathen."

"What is given of grace must be kept by grace, or it is confounded and taken away."

"A name once holy is no safety where the LORD is forsaken for the high places."
